display.purpose: Front-page lead headline only. 800, 34 to 48px fluid, 1.15, max 22ch.

headline.purpose: Article headline on each piece page; sign-in title.

title.purpose: Section titles, In this issue headlines, article subheads (2em above, 0.6em below), pull quotes (700), Keep label; standfirst at 400 / 1.4 in ink-2. Largest text size lifts it to 1.75rem.

body.purpose: Reading text, one ragged-right column of 64ch or less, no hyphenation, word spacing 0.08em. Reader sizes 17/19/22/25px via --fs-body; first paragraph x1.08. Wide spacing: 0.12em / 0.16em / line 2 / paragraphs 2em.

label.purpose: Bylines, captions, buttons, chips, band, dateline, ears, folios, meta. 400 or 700, 16px. The floor: nothing smaller.

nameplate.purpose: Grenze Gotisch SemiBold as an outlined SVG path in currentColor (src/lib/nameplate.ts). The only blackletter; min 24px high; 30px app bar and mini front, 48-72px Desk, 60-88px front masthead, 96px sign-in.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.value: outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 3px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 7px var(--marigold)
shadows.purpose: Every :focus-visible. A flat marigold ring, not elevation. --focus is ink, marigold in night.

shadows.name: current-bar
shadows.purpose: Current Desk nav item and selected settings chip. A flat fill bar, not elevation.

motion.name: page-turn
motion.purpose: Sheet fades out, next page lands at the top (or the ribbon's paragraph), fades in. No flip. Instant under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

motion.name: disclosure
motion.purpose: More on this topic chevron rotates 90 degrees when open.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Desk nav short labels; Keep row and bind bar stack; card actions become a grid.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Gutter 16px; masthead stacks, ears become one inline line; app bar drops where and Print; turn bar shows only Previous/Next.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Skyline, lead grid, In this issue and clipping cards collapse to one column.

rules.oxford: hr: height 7px; two linear-gradient bands of --ink, 4px top and 1px bottom (.flip reverses). Print: 2.4pt / 2pt gap / 0.6pt.
rules.endMark: 0.6em square, --marigold fill, 1px --ink outline, after the last word of each piece.
rules.ribbon: assets/ribbon.svg, V-notched strip. 14x38 in the ribbon note; 16x44 hanging 36px left of the stopped paragraph (10x30 at 14px on phones).

print.body: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next Regular 12pt / 18pt leading, ragged right, one column
print.note: Quire's note 11pt in a marigold-soft box
print.folio: 0.6pt rule; Quire 9pt Bold left, Page n 9pt right, muted
print.colors: ink, ink-2, muted, rule, marigold, marigold-soft (newsprint values)
print.extras: front sheet with outlined nameplate + Oxford rule; end mark per piece; source QR code

components.name: Outlined Button
components.description: Default action: Read the full piece, Keep. 2px ink frame, marigold-soft on hover.

components.description: The page's one reversed element: Create issue, Sign in.

components.description: Labelled field: 2px ink frame, 52px, body-size text, error as icon + bold sentence.

components.name: Settings Chip
components.description: Reading settings radio: hairline frame; selected gets ink frame and a marigold inset bar.
components.css: .ds-chip { position: relative; display: inline-block; font-family: 'Atkinson Hyperlegible Next', Verdana, sans-serif; } .ds-chip input { position: absolute; opacity: 0; inset: 0; margin: 0; cursor: pointer; } .ds-chip span { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; min-height: 44px; padding: 6px 12px; border: 2px solid var(--line, #cfc6aa); border-radius: 2px; background: var(--paper, #f7f2df); color: var(--ink, #22201b); font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.2; } .ds-chip input:checked + span { border-color: var(--ink, #22201b); box-shadow: inset 0 -5px 0 var(--marigold, #f2b705); font-weight: 700; } .ds-chip input:focus-visible + span { outline: 3px solid var(--focus, #22201b); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-swatch { width: 18px; height: 18px; border-radius: 50%; border: 1px solid rgba(34,32,27,0.45); }

components.name: Masthead

components.css: .ds-mast { color: var(--ink, #22201b); font-family: 'Atkinson Hyperlegible Next', Verdana, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.02em; padding-top: 20px; } .ds-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto 1fr; gap: 24px; align-items: center; } .ds-ear { margin: 0; width: 12rem; border: 1px solid var(--ink, #22201b); padding: 10px 12px; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.4; } .ds-ear strong { display: block; } .ds-r { justify-self: end; } .ds-plate { display: block; height: 72px; width: auto; color: var(--ink, #22201b); } .ds-oxford { border: 0; height: 7px; margin: 14px 0 0; background: linear-gradient(var(--ink, #22201b), var(--ink, #22201b)) top / 100% 4px no-repeat, linear-gradient(var(--ink, #22201b), var(--ink, #22201b)) bottom / 100% 1px no-repeat; } .ds-dateline { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 4px 24px; margin: 6px 0 0; padding: 8px 14px; background: var(--band-ink, #22201b); color: var(--band-text, #f7f2df); font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.4; }

narrative.overview:
Each bound issue reads as a British Sunday paper made for one dyslexic reader. The front page shows what is inside at a glance; every other piece gets its own page, opening on a marigold section band, set in one calm ragged-right column. The newspaper is the frame; the reading is plain. The furniture is traditional: an outlined blackletter nameplate, Oxford rules (thick over thin), ears, an ink dateline bar, section bands, folios, an end mark. The reading text drops the tradition's habits and follows the BDA Dyslexia Style Guide instead: sans-serif, left-aligned, one column, no italics, no capital labels, off-white paper.

Density is calm. One family at five sizes, hairline rules instead of boxes, flat paper with no texture. The reader owns the paper. Six tints, four text sizes and two spacing settings are applied as data-* attributes on <html> before first paint, and every surface (the reading pages and the Desk) is built from the tint-swappable tokens. The signature interaction is the ribbon: the issue remembers where you stopped and offers to take you back.

The product refuses the read-later list and the dense justified broadsheet.
keyCharacteristics: Flat newsprint paper. Ink rules, no shadows, 2px corners.
Marigold is only ever a fill: band, ribbon, ticks, current-tab bar, end mark, selection, focus halo.
One reversed (paper-on-ink) element per reading page marks what matters most.
One sans family, five sizes, nothing below 16px.
Every colour is a token that swaps per reader tint, including the mat behind photographs.

rules.name: The Fill-Only Marigold Rule
rules.body: Marigold is a fill, never text on paper and never the nameplate's colour. Anything set on marigold is ink.

rules.name: The Every-Colour-Is-A-Token Rule
rules.body: A new surface uses --paper, --sheet, --mat, --line, --line-2, --ink*, --muted, --link*, --band-*, never a literal hex, so all six tints and night work without extra code.

rules.name: The No Status Colour Rule
rules.body: There is no red, green or pink anywhere. A problem is the drawn alert icon plus a bold sentence in ink. Waiting is the clock icon plus the step in words.

rules.name: The Five Sizes Rule
rules.body: Display, Headline, Subhead, Body, Small. That is the whole scale. The only derived size is the x1.08 opening paragraph.

rules.name: The Upright Rule
rules.body: No italics anywhere. em, i, cite and blockquote are set upright, and emphasis becomes weight 700, including the source's own italics.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headlines and labels are sentence case with no negative tracking (headings track 0, word spacing 0.04em, text-wrap: balance). There are no capital-letter labels and no small caps.

rules.name: The One Blackletter Rule
rules.body: The nameplate is the only blackletter, always the outlined path, never under 24px high (app bar 30px, mini front 30px, Desk masthead 48-72px, front masthead 60-88px, sign-in 96px).

rules.name: The Columns Drop, Type Never Shrinks Rule
rules.body: On phones every grid collapses to one column. Type sizes stay the same, and labels shorten instead.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows, no texture, no grain, no gradients except the two-band Oxford rule. To lift something, step the paper (sheet) or reverse it (ink).

rules.name: The One Reversed Element Rule
rules.body: Each reading page has exactly one paper-on-ink element: the dateline bar on the front page, and the primary button where it is the page's main action (Create issue on the bind bar). Everything else is outlined or ruled.

dos: Do build every new surface from the tint tokens (--paper, --sheet, --mat, --line, --line-2, --ink, --muted, --link, --band-ink, --band-text) and check it in all six papers, Night included.
Do put photographs on --mat, whole (object-fit: contain), capped at 26rem on a page, 18rem in the front-page lead and 12rem on a card, and never inside running text.
Do keep reading text in one ragged-right column of 64ch or less, with paragraph gaps from --para.
Do underline every link (1px, 0.28em offset; 2px on hover) so the cue is never colour alone.
Do pair every icon with a word and every state with an icon plus a sentence.
Do keep targets at 44px minimum, and 48px for buttons and page turns.
Do mark rank by reversal (one ink element per page) and by Oxford rules, not by colour or size jumps.
Do fade the page turn at 220ms and drop it under reduced motion.
donts: Don't set text in marigold on paper, colour the nameplate marigold, or use marigold as a large decorative ground beyond the band.
Don't use italics, capital-letter labels, eyebrows above headlines, justified text, hyphenation, drop caps or multi-column reading text.
Don't add a sixth type size or anything below 16px.
Don't use drop shadows, textures, grain or glassy effects. box-shadow is allowed only as the flat marigold focus halo or the inset current bar.
Don't use red, green or pink, for status or anything else.
Don't set any other text in blackletter, or put the nameplate on a photograph.
Don't crop source figures or invent standfirsts, ear facts or reading times. Show what the source and the issue actually hold.
Don't use the ribbon as decoration. It means "you stopped here".
